tool: Ahrefs Keywords Explorer, keywords-explorer-overview, one call per candidate country
extends: market-expansion-ranking-2026-10-05.json, which measured en-AU, tr-TR, id-ID, es-MX, th-TH, ko-KR, vi-VN, de-AT, ru-RU and ar-SA. Those rows are not re-measured and not restated here.
what_this_pass_adds: eight wealthy or high-demand candidates that had never been measured, chosen on the brief's priority list: the four Nordic markets, Israel, Czechia, Greece and the UAE.
the_criterion_the_previous_pass_establis: a new market in an EXISTING language cannot open a URL. The URL space is language-scoped, so en-CA, en-IE, en-NZ, en-SG, de-AT, de-CH, fr-BE, nl-BE and fr-CA can only take ownership of entities an existing market in that language does not already claim. The offline market-URL experiment measured that yield directly on en-AU and es-MX and it was ZERO net new valid pages. de-AT measured 1,450 total volume in the 2026-10-05 pass, which says the same thing from the demand side. So every candidate ranked here is a NEW LANGUAGE.
the_new_finding_of_this_pass: candidate markets split into two kinds and only one of them yields pages. In the first kind the per-city attraction family is ALIVE, so every city is a page: Hebrew reads 3,800 on Jerusalem and 1,900 on Tel Aviv and still 800 on Rome and 450 on Paris; Finnish reads 2,100 on Tampere, 1,500 on Helsinki, 800 on Barcelona, 700 on Rome, all at difficulty 0 or 1; Greek reads 800 on Rome, 600 on Paris, 500 on Barcelona, 400 on Athens, every one at difficulty 0. In the second kind only the GENERIC connectivity intent lives and the per-city family is dead: Czech reads esim 10,000 and esim karta 1,700 and then praha co videt 90, brno 100, rim 50; Arabic in the UAE reads esim 5,300 and then paris 10, london 40, turkey 20. That is the Turkish pattern from 2026-10-05 repeating, and it is the single best predictor of page yield in this whole exercise. A market of the second kind can sell a SIM and cannot carry an atlas.

candidates.family_kind: ALIVE both domestically and for destinations
candidates.source_coverage: Israel is NOT captured in OSM and hewiki marks have not been fetched
candidates.duplicate_risk: none, a new script and a new URL space
candidates.monetization: esim at 14,000 and CPC 130 cents is the largest eSIM volume of any candidate measured in either pass
candidates.why: the strongest combination measured: the largest connectivity volume, a city family alive at difficulty 0 to 3 for domestic AND destination cities, and a wealthy market. It needs a capture and a sitelink pass before it can produce one page.

candidates.family_kind: ALIVE, and note the destination city beats the domestic one: Barcelona 700 against Stockholm 500
candidates.source_coverage: Sweden is NOT captured and svwiki marks have not been fetched
candidates.why: a wealthy market with a live family in both directions and thailand resa at 4,200 showing the destination intent is real. Second only to Hebrew on measured volume.

candidates.family_kind: the CLEANEST family fit measured anywhere: one template, nähtävyydet, carries every city tested, domestic and destination, at difficulty 0 or 1
candidates.a_measurement_trap_worth_recording: the bare keyword esim could NOT be used for Finland. esim. is the standard Finnish abbreviation for 'for example', so its volume measures a word and not a product. esim kortti, e sim kortti and esim liittymä were used instead. Measuring Finland with the template every other market uses would have reported a false five-figure connectivity reading.
candidates.source_coverage: Finland is NOT captured and fiwiki marks have not been fetched
candidates.why: lower total volume than Sweden but the most uniform family, which matters more for page yield than a single large head term: a template that works at difficulty 0 across every city is a template that scales to the whole gazetteer.

candidates.family_kind: ALIVE, thinner than Sweden at the city level
candidates.monetization: the HIGHEST CPC measured in either pass: esim at 200 cents and esim kort at 180
candidates.source_coverage: Denmark is NOT captured and dawiki marks have not been fetched
candidates.why: the best monetization per click of any candidate and a live if thinner family. Ranked below Finland because Danish city volumes are smaller and the second city, Aarhus, reads 100.

candidates.family_kind: SPLIT, and this is why the phrasing has to be measured per language rather than translated. The severdigheter template is dead in Norwegian - Oslo 70, Bergen 50, Barcelona 60, Tokyo ZERO - while ting å gjøre i oslo reads 3,200. The same concept, one phrasing worth a page and one worth nothing.
candidates.source_coverage: Norway is NOT captured and nowiki marks have not been fetched
candidates.why: a wealthy market whose connectivity half is solid, but only one city phrasing works and it was measured on one city. Admitting Norway means measuring ting å gjøre i X across a proper city sample first, because a 3,200 reading on the capital tells you nothing about the twentieth city.

candidates.family_kind: ALIVE and OUTWARD: every destination city beats the domestic capital. Rome 800 and Paris 600 against Athens 400. Difficulty is ZERO on all six.
candidates.source_coverage: Greece is NOT captured. Greek destination demand for other countries is however already usable through the destination table if elwiki marks are fetched.
candidates.duplicate_risk: none, a new script and a new URL space
candidates.why: the lowest total volume of the live-family group, but difficulty zero on every city keyword and a clearly outward-facing market, which is the commercial shape this product wants. A cheap market to enter if the mark pass is cheap.

candidates.family_kind: DEAD at city level. 11,700 of the 13,390 measured volume sits in two generic eSIM keywords; the attraction template reads 90 on the CAPITAL.
candidates.priority: NOT RECOMMENDED as an atlas market
candidates.why: the Turkish and Portuguese pattern in its purest form. Czech carries real money for a SIM and no measured appetite for a city page. Admitting it would build a URL space for a family that reads 90 on Prague. Recorded as measured and refused, which is evidence, where never asking would have been an absence.

candidates.family_kind: DOMESTIC ONLY and thin. Dubai 800 at difficulty 31, Abu Dhabi 500, and then Paris 10, London 40, Turkey 20, Thailand 20. The outward intent that a Gulf travel market should have is not in these numbers.
candidates.source_coverage: the UAE IS partly captured already, which is the one point in its favour
candidates.why: confirms ar-SA from 2026-10-05, which read 1,630. Two Arabic markets measured in two passes and both are connectivity-only. The wealth of the market is real and the measured page demand is not, and the brief's own rule is to measure rather than assume. A different Arabic phrasing may exist and this measurement does not claim to have found the ceiling: it claims that the obvious phrasings read 10 to 40 on the destinations a Dubai resident actually flies to.

ranking_for_materialisation: 1. he-IL  largest connectivity volume measured, family alive in both directions
2. sv-SE  wealthy, family alive, destination beats domestic
3. fi-FI  the most uniform family of any candidate, one template at difficulty 0
4. da-DK  the highest CPC measured anywhere, family alive but thinner
5. nb-NO  solid connectivity, one working city phrasing, needs a city sample first
6. el-GR  smallest of the live group, difficulty zero everywhere, outward facing
cs-CZ  measured and refused: a SIM market, not an atlas market
ar-AE  measured and refused: domestic only and thin, confirming ar-SA
what_none_of_these_can_do_yet: not one of the six recommended markets can produce a single page today. Each needs two things that are not downloads of demand data: a Wikipedia sitelink pass in its language, to supply the per-entity mark that is half two of every gate, and an OSM capture of its own country for the domestic half. That is the same blocking dependency ko-KR carries. So this ranking is an order of work, not an inventory gain, and it is not counted toward the candidate total anywhere.
what_this_does_not_do: it does not sample a SERP in any of these markets. The brief admits a market on measured demand AND real local phrasing AND a verified SERP, and ko-KR is the standing proof of why: it passed demand by the widest margin of any candidate and failed the SERP by the widest margin. No market here is admitted; six are recommended for a SERP pass in the order above.
licence_and_provenance: Ahrefs Keywords Explorer via the Ahrefs API v3 on 2026-10-06, one call per candidate country code. Volumes are Ahrefs monthly estimates for that country and CPC is in USD cents as the API returns it. Every number here is a row the API returned; keywords it returned nothing for are recorded as absent rather than as zero.
